text: The nonlinear parameter gamma of a 450x220 nm silicon strip waveguide (~290 W^-1 m^-1) is roughly 5000x larger than that of standard single-mode fiber. What is the primary reason?
choices: Silicon's linear refractive index is 5000x larger than glass
The silicon waveguide has much lower propagation loss
Its mode is confined to an effective area (~0.14 um^2) hundreds of times smaller than SMF's (~85 um^2), and silicon's n2 is also larger
The silicon waveguide is much longer than a fiber span
explanation: gamma = n2*omega/(c*A_eff), so the ~600x smaller effective mode area of the silicon strip plus its larger nonlinear index n2 drive gamma up by ~5000x. Silicon's linear index (3.48) is only ~2.4x that of glass, not 5000x; loss and length do not appear in gamma at all.
